children: founder Zvi Schreiber took to LinkedIn to call on shareholders to shake up the board.

Schreiber said he stayed silent for six months after exiting the board when it declared 2026 a transition year and announced it was "deliberately sequencing" growth, with a goal to reach breakeven by cutting rather than growing.

"I stayed silent for more than six months, hoping they would prove me wrong. Several times I wrote to the board privately. They declined to course correct," highlighted Schreiber. "Last quarter, revenue grew 3% year on year — no more than inflation — against the company's model of 25–30% a year, and Q3 is guided to 1–2%. Solutions, the segment the board pivoted to, shrank 4%," he noted.
Schreiber thinks the good news is that the situation at Freightos
is fixable and aims for the company to return to platform-first, AI-native growth, starting with relaunching the Marketplace and a rebuilt team.

Schreiber founded Freightos in January 2012 after identifying international freight as a large but technology-lagging market: rates, quotes, and bookings were often handled through opaque, labor-intensive processes. Freightos began with software for freight forwarders, launched beta customers in October 2012, and commercially launched in March 2013.

went public through a merger with the SPAC Gesher I Acquisition Corp. on January 25, 2023. In December 2025, Freightos announced a CEO succession process. Schreiber’s transition out of the CEO role took effect on January 31, and he left the board in February.
are down more than 40% since Schreiber left the CEO position.

title: Freightos founder calls for a board reset amid share price struggle
